subject: Urgent: Amplified retry traffic from PayHarbor causing 5xx/429 spike
messages:
From: Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@payharbor.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@payharbor.com, rita@payharbor.com
Date: 2027-04-11T15:12:00Z
Subject: Sudden 5xx/429 spike after morning deploy — please advise

Hi Laura,

We're seeing a large spike in 5xx and 429 responses from Redwood since our 08:00 deploy this morning. Latency is up from ~120ms to ~850ms on average and throughput is flapping; our dashboards show a sharp increase in request retries from our fleet. This is affecting checkout for ~12% of users — we need help triaging immediately.

Relevant details:
- Region: us-east-1
- SDK version: pay-sdk-js v2.1.3 (we recently rolled out)
- Typical qps: 1800; observed burst to ~6k (sustained for ~15m)

I've attached a small sample of request IDs and response headers. Can you confirm whether there was any capacity or routing change on Redwood's side?

Thanks — Michael

--
Michael Jenkins
Site Reliability Lead, PayHarbor

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@payharbor.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike after morning deploy — please advise

Hi Michael — sorry you're hitting this. I'm escalating and looping in SRE/Platform (Marcus, Grace, Vivek) to investigate immediately.

Initial asks to speed triage:
- Can you share a sample span/trace id for a problematic request?
- Any retries configured on the client SDK (count/backoff/jitter)?
- A direct contact for a bridge if we need to jump on a call (I'll hold a slot at 16:00 UTC).

We're standing by and will surface findings in-line.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike after morning deploy — please advise

Quick snapshot from our side after sampling 5000 recent requests tied to PayHarbor:
- Elevated 429s originating from the same small set of client IPs and identical idempotency keys (suggests retry amplification).
- A substantial fraction of 5xx responses correlate with queue saturation on the serving tier (queue length spiked ~10x).
- No scheduled capacity changes in us-east-1; autoscaler behaved as expected but couldn't keep up with the burst pattern.

I've attached redwood-logs-sample-0411.txt with trace ids and headers. Early hypothesis: client-side retry behavior may be aggressively re-sending identical requests without exponential backoff/jitter, causing an amplification loop when transient errors return.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Rita Alvarez <rita@payharbor.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@payharbor.com>, ops@payharbor.com
Date: 2027-04-11T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike after morning deploy — please advise

Thanks Marcus — that aligns with what we see. We shipped a change this morning that updated our internal retry wrapper. We set retries=5 and used a fixed 200ms sleep between attempts to reduce latency on DB calls.

Excerpt from our wrapper:
```
for (let i = 0; i < retries; i++) {
  try { return await call(); } catch (e) { await sleep(200); }
}
```
We did not add jitter or exponential backoff — the intention was to keep retries tight for quick transient failures. I can temporarily flip this back if you recommend.

— Rita

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Rita Alvarez <rita@payharbor.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike after morning deploy — please advise

Thanks for the snippet, Rita. That pattern explains amplification: identical requests retried with a fixed, small sleep will repeatedly hit the service in lockstep if a subset of clients experience transient errors. Without jitter or exponential backoff, retries create correlated bursts that the autoscaler can't smooth.

Immediate mitigations we can do from Redwood side:
- Enable a short, conservative emergency quota for PayHarbor to limit burst amplification (5 min window)
- Honor Retry-After strictly and surface 429s with Retry-After to clients where applicable
- Patch SDK to send Retry-After aware backoffs and add jitter in next minor release (we can provide a hotfix patch for PayHarbor to apply now)

Rita / Michael — can you rollback the wrapper to use exponential backoff + jitter (e.g., base=200ms, multiplier=2, jitter=0.5) while we stand up the emergency quota? That will stop amplification immediately. I'm attaching a mitigation-playbook.pdf with step-by-step actions.

Connor O'Brien
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@payharbor.com>, Rita Alvarez <rita@payharbor.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike after morning deploy — please advise

Michael / Rita — thanks for the quick detail. Our recommended immediate path:
1) PayHarbor: roll back to exponential backoff + jitter (Connor suggested params).
2) Redwood: apply a temporary emergency quota and enable stricter honoring of Retry-After headers.
3) Joint call at 16:00 UTC for final handoff — I'll open the bridge and share notes.

If you agree, we'll proceed and confirm once traffic returns to normal.

Laura

From: Rita Alvarez <rita@payharbor.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Jenkins <michael.jenkins@payharbor.com>, ops@payharbor.com
Date: 2027-04-12T22:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 spike after morning deploy — please advise

Update: we reverted the retry wrapper yesterday afternoon to exponential backoff with jitter and deployed a hotfix. We also applied the patch you provided (payharbor-retry-config.patch.txt). Traffic stabilized within ~10 minutes and 5xx/429 rates returned to baseline.

Thanks to the Redwood team for the mitigation playbook and for standing by — we'll follow up with a postmortem and schedule a follow-up to roll the SDK fix into our next release.

Rita Alvarez
Staff Engineer, PayHarbor
